records.headline: The Pompeii wardrobe that stayed closed for nearly 2,000 years
records.discoverSummary: A wooden cabinet preserved at Pompeii offered archaeologists a rare look at what people kept in a Roman home. Its contents help tell a smaller, more personal story than the city's famous ruins: the objects and beliefs that accompanied ordinary life.

records.headline: A flute from ancient Troy brings the past into earshot
records.discoverSummary: Archaeologists excavating Troy uncovered a bone flute in a layer dating to the eighth century BCE. The discovery adds something unexpected to the picture of ancient Troy: a surviving musical instrument, not just walls and weapons.

records.headline: A teenager finds an ancient Greek coin near Berlin
records.discoverSummary: A 13-year-old's discovery in a field outside Berlin led researchers to a bronze coin minted in ancient Troy. Scholars believe it is the first ancient Greek artifact unearthed in Berlin, although how it traveled there remains a mystery.

records.headline: Two stars merged—and astronomers reconstructed the story
records.discoverSummary: In the Andromeda galaxy, a smaller star spiraled into a larger companion. By combining observations from the James Webb Space Telescope and other instruments, researchers reconstructed the merger and what happened afterward.

records.headline: The deep-sea golden orb finally has an identity
records.discoverSummary: When ocean explorers spotted a golden sphere almost two miles below the surface near Alaska in 2023, they couldn't identify it immediately. A later investigation found it was the remnants of a giant deep-sea anemone—an answer that took years to uncover.

records.headline: Why astronomers call these galaxies 'platypuses'
records.discoverSummary: A group of distant galaxies combines features astronomers don't usually see together. The research team compared the odd combination to a platypus—an unexpected mix that may offer clues to early galaxy formation.

records.headline: Golf's rulebook has been evolving since 1744
records.discoverSummary: Golf's early written rules date to 1744, but the game hasn't stood still. Equipment, playing conditions, and the way competitions are organized have all shaped revisions over centuries.

records.headline: The early baseball game remembered for much more than its score
records.discoverSummary: A recorded 1846 game in Hoboken ended with a lopsided 23–1 score, but its lasting significance is in the organized rules and game structure that helped shape modern baseball.

records.headline: A sloth discovers the joys of a water hose
records.discoverSummary: The Smithsonian's National Zoo introduced Olive, a two-toed sloth, with footage of her enjoying water-hose enrichment. It's a brief, playful glimpse of animal care—and a lighter discovery for a morning edition.

records.headline: An 1899 silent comedy still offers a mischievous moment
records.discoverSummary: Long before social-media clips, short films were experimenting with visual mischief. The Library of Congress catalog preserves an early Edison-era film titled Little Mischief, offering readers a playful detour into the earliest years of screen comedy.
